writeup: TIC 176348607 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.965244 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces an 8.36 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal carries a high detection significance of 160.7 in the BLS periodogram, and pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 76.0, though the centroid offset of 1.3 arcseconds warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, which suggests the true orbital period may be twice the initially measured value, a quirk that should be considered in any follow-up analysis.
